text: Hi, I need help writing a firm but polite message to my builder. Our kitchen extension was due to finish on 14 March but the roof is still not on. Tadeusz Wrona quoted 18,500 pounds and I have already paid 12,000 pounds in two instalments. Tadeusz says the delay is because his bricklayer, Ayodele Fashola, fell ill for two weeks, which I accept, but I won't pay the next 3,000-pound stage until the roof is on. You can reach me on 07700 900314 or at imani.reyes@example.com. My job reference with his firm is JOB-55291. Please keep the tone calm and say that I'm happy to meet on site on Friday.
task: Draft a calm but firm email to the builder about the delay and the withheld payment, keeping the amounts and conditions exactly as I stated them.

text: My neighbour, Halldóra Sigurðardóttir, has lodged an objection to our planning application for a loft conversion. Her letter says the dormer would overlook her garden and cut light to her kitchen. The council case officer, Mr Parminder Gill, told us the decision is due by 28 May and that the application number is PA/2026/0417. Our architect, Bui Thi Hanh, thinks the objection is weak because the dormer sits 2.5 metres back from the boundary, not 1.5 metres as Halldóra claims. I can be reached on 07700 900462 and the address on the form is 14 Alder Rise, Kettering. Please help me draft a short reply to the case officer that corrects the distance and does not sound hostile.
task: Draft a short, courteous reply to the council case officer that corrects the distance the objector gave and notes the decision date.

text: I'm switching energy suppliers and want to check I'm not missing a step. My current supplier is Brightleaf Energy and my account number is BL-7720-4491. My meter readings on 3 November were 48,215 kWh for electricity and 6,830 cubic metres for gas. The new supplier, Cinder Power, promised a fixed rate of 24.1p per kWh for 12 months with no exit fee, but only if the switch completes before 30 November. My housemate, Sapna Kulkarni, is the named account holder, so she has to approve the switch by phone on 07700 900228. Her email for the paperwork is sapna.k@example.net. I would also like to know whether I should photograph both meters on the day the switch goes through.
task: Give me a checklist for completing the switch, plus a short final-reading email to the old supplier that uses my readings and the deadline.

text: Subject: boiler service booking. Hello, our annual boiler service is booked for 11 December between 8am and 12pm, but I'll only be home after 10am so please don't arrive before then. The engineer, Kimani Njoroge, serviced it last year and noted the pressure was low at 0.8 bar and recommended topping up to 1.2 bar. Our landlord, Elias Haddad, pays the service fee of 85 pounds but wants the certificate emailed to him at elias.haddad@example.org. The booking reference is HB-90381 and the tenancy address is 9 Marlow Terrace, Leeds. Please help me turn this into a short confirmation message to the heating firm.
task: Write a short confirmation message to the heating firm covering the arrival window, the pressure note and where the certificate goes.

text: Notes for the bathroom refit. Plumber Oluwaseun Adeyemi starts on 2 June and needs the old bath out by Sunday. Tiler Mirela Constantin can only do the floor if the plumber has finished first, otherwise she will come back on 16 June. Electrician quote from Ferenc Szabo is 640 pounds for the extractor fan and two spotlights, excluding the 20 percent VAT. I paid Oluwaseun a 200-pound deposit last week. Ferenc wants the balance paid to IBAN GB00 FAKE 0000 1122 3344 55 within seven days of finishing. Please turn these notes into a week-by-week schedule and show me which jobs depend on which.

text: Please help me turn this into a complaint to my old energy supplier. I closed account number 30-884-217 on 9 September when I moved out, but they sent a final bill for 312.40 pounds that includes 41 days after I left. The adviser I spoke to, Gwenllian Pugh, agreed on the phone that the closing reading was 21,904 and said she would reissue the bill within five working days. That was three weeks ago and nothing has arrived. My new address is Flat 3, 22 Henshaw Road, Cardiff and my email is tegan.morris@example.net. I want the bill recalculated and a written apology, and I will go to the ombudsman if it is not fixed by 30 October.
task: Write a formal complaint letter to the energy supplier setting out the billing error, the promised reissue that never came and what I want done by the deadline.

text: Hi Zainab, following your call I've pulled together the details for the porch. The planning officer, Dariusz Lewandowski, said on 6 October that a porch under 3 square metres and more than 2 metres from the highway should count as permitted development. Ours is 2.8 square metres and sits 4.2 metres from the road. He also said the conservation area does not apply to our street, not Fenwick Lane, which is the next one over. The fee is 258 pounds if we do need to apply. Please check my reading and tell me what I still need to confirm. Mobile: 07700 900587. Rohan Bhatt
task: Check whether the porch measurements fit what the planning officer said, and list anything I still need to confirm.

text: Comparing two quotes for the roof repair. Builder one, Anselm Okwuosa, quoted 7,400 pounds including scaffolding and says he can start on 19 January. Builder two, Katja Virtanen, quoted 6,150 pounds but scaffolding is extra at roughly 900 pounds, and she can only start in March. Anselm's price includes a 10-year guarantee; Katja offers 5 years. My mother-in-law, Fatima Rahimi, is lending us up to 2,000 pounds, but only if the work starts before the end of February. Anselm's mobile is 07700 900163 and Katja's is 07700 900741. Which quote fits best, and what should I ask each of them?
task: Compare the two roof quotes on total cost, start date and guarantee, and suggest questions for each builder.

text: I need to chase my home emergency cover about the boiler. The boiler stopped heating on 2 February; I called Hearthguard on the same day and the engineer, Bartosz Michalak, came on 4 February, not 3 February as their email says. He replaced the diverter valve and said the part is covered, but the callout excess of 75 pounds is still payable. Policy no. HG-2209-6613. They then charged me 150 pounds on my card, which is double the excess. I'd like the extra 75 pounds refunded. My partner, Eilidh Rennie, took the call on the second day, so mention that she can confirm the time. You can email me on cathal.dunne@example.com.
task: Draft a complaint to the cover provider that corrects their visit date, explains the double charge and asks for the refund.

I spoke with the customer's procurement lead, Hamid Zarei, who confirmed they want to renew 120 seats for another 12 months, not the 150 we assumed in the forecast. task: Turn these deal notes into a three-bullet summary for my manager with the seat count, the deadline and who owns each next step.

text: Quick summary of who owes what for the garage conversion so I can send it to the group. The total quote is 14,400 pounds. Brother-in-law Cormac Deasy agreed to pay 40 percent, not a third as I first wrote. Jamila Idowu is paying nothing towards the build but will cover the 1,200-pound planning fee. Cormac only pays his share if the council approves the plans by 15 August; if they refuse, nobody pays the builder, Sione Taufa, anything beyond the 300-pound survey he has already done. I am covering the rest, and I haven't asked Jamila for anything else. Please write a clear message to all three that keeps each person's share and condition exactly right.
task: Write a clear message to the group that states each person's share and condition exactly, including what happens if the plans are refused.

text: Notes from the planning meeting. Architect Ines Carvalho thinks we probably will not need full planning permission for the garden room, but she was clear it depends on keeping the height at 2.5 metres or less. Our neighbour Obinna Eze says the council told him the opposite, that any outbuilding within 2 metres of a boundary needs consent. I don't know which of them is right and I haven't spoken to the council myself. Obinna also says he won't object if we move the room 1 metre further from his fence. Ines says moving it is fine but costs about 600 pounds extra. I want a short list of what we still need to confirm and who we should ask, without turning any maybe into a definite.
task: Make a short list of what I still need to confirm and who to ask, keeping every hedge and condition as stated.

text: Message to my sister about the energy switch. Dear Maren, I told you the new tariff was 27p per kWh, but that's wrong: it's 23p per kWh, with a standing charge of 52p a day. Our flatmate Idris Bakare thinks we'd save roughly 180 pounds a year, though he hasn't included the standing charge, so I wouldn't trust his figure yet. Teuila Faleolo from the supplier said the switch takes up to 21 days and that we must not cancel the old direct debit ourselves. I still have to decide whether to switch before our current fixed deal ends on 31 January; I will only switch if the exit fee is zero. Can you help me put this clearly?
task: Rewrite this as a clear message to my sister that corrects the earlier figure and shows which numbers are firm and which are only estimates.

text: Update on the flat's boiler service. The landlord, Bronwen Aldous, did not book the service this year; I did, and she will reimburse the 92 pounds only if I send the invoice by Friday. The engineer, Jabu Mokoena, found no leak but did say the flue seal is worn and should be replaced within six months. He did not condemn the boiler, whatever the letting agent claims. Our other tenant, Lorcan Whelan, says he was told the carbon monoxide alarm needs a new battery, but I checked and it was fine. Can you draft a note to my landlord that gets the facts right: what was and wasn't found, what the invoice deadline is and whether the alarm works?
task: Draft a note to my landlord that states what the engineer found and did not find, the invoice deadline and whether the alarm works.

text: I'm planning a small single-storey rear extension and I've been reading the Planning Portal guidance on permitted development alongside Approved Document L of the Building Regulations. The guidance says some rear extensions can be built without a full application, but only within certain size limits and not in every conservation area. I also noticed that any new electrical circuits have to follow BS 7671 and be notified under Part P, and that gas work must be done by someone on the Gas Safe Register. Ofgem publishes the energy price cap, which I want to understand before choosing a heat pump over a new gas boiler. Can you explain, in plain terms, which of these rules apply to the build itself and which apply to the heating choice?
task: Explain in plain terms which of these rules apply to the build and which to the heating choice.

text: I'm building a monthly sales pipeline report and want to make sure the definitions are standard. We use stages named Qualified, Proposal, Negotiation and Closed Won, and I plan to report win rate as closed-won deals divided by all closed deals. Our CRM can export to CSV, and the BI tool loads that file nightly. Last week one export failed with an HTTP 504 error and a retry fixed it, so I'd like a simple retry policy. I also want to confirm that our customer data handling follows GDPR Article 28 and that the vendor's ISO 27001 certificate covers the hosting region. Please suggest a clean layout for the report with a short glossary of the stage names and metrics, and a sensible retry setting.
task: Suggest a clean report layout with a short glossary of the stage names and metrics, plus a sensible retry setting for the nightly export.

text: Our weekly pipeline export to the BI tool is failing with a 403. This is the call I run from the scheduler: curl -s -H "X-Api-Key: qa_9d41b7e0_fake" "https://crm.internal.test/v2/deals?stage=negotiation&owner=emea" -o deals.json. The response body is {"error":"forbidden","detail":"key scope missing deals:read"}. The BI tool just shows an empty file and the scheduler log says the job exited with code 22. This worked until Friday, when ops changed the scopes. For context, the largest open renewal is for Brightwater Marine at 1.4 million dollars, and finance asked that it not leave the building. Which scope or header change should I request, and is there anything wrong with the query string itself?
task: Diagnose the 403 and tell me which scope or header change to request; the deal details are not needed.
